subject: Shopwise model-fit recap & proposed A/B matrix
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Jensen <claire@shopwise.com>, Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@shopwise.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-30T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Shopwise call recap + proposed model-fit next steps

Hi Claire / Tom —

Great speaking with you today. Quick recap and the concrete next steps we discussed so the team is aligned: 

Summary from our call:
- Use case: Search result reranking across desktop + mobile catalog, focus on reducing poor-click rate and improving top-3 relevance for merchandising promos.
- Current constraints: 90 ms P95 latency target for inline reranking, budget guidance: target incremental inference <= $0.003 per query.
- Success metrics: NDCG@10 lift target >= +5% and MRR lift target >= +6% versus your baseline model.

Immediate asks we agreed on:
1) We’ll run a lightweight model-fit evaluation on a 10k labeled holdout you can provide (or we can sample from your 90-day logs).
2) We’ll share prompt sets and the first-pass rerank templates for your review.
3) Proposed canary A/B matrix and roll-out plan for live testing.

Initial model suggestions (based on your data profile + latency needs):
- Variant A (low-latency): LlamaX-7B-quant with optimized KV caching — best cost/latency balance for mobile traffic.
- Variant B (quality-focused): Falcon-40B-ptq, with a trimmed prompt set for ranking context; expect higher NDCG but higher unit cost.
- Variant C (fallback): Distil-rerank-3B (cheap, fast) for heavy burst windows.

I’ve attached the prompt_set_v1 and a draft AB matrix for internal review. Neha / Marissa will run the NDCG/MRR snapshot once we have your sample.

Next steps
- Claire: share a 10k labeled sample or grant read access to a 90-day export by Tuesday 6/1.
- Redwood: we’ll produce an NDCG/MRR snapshot and a recommended A/B matrix by 6/2.
- Schedule: propose 30-min follow-up on 6/3 to review results and finalize canary timing.

Thanks — looking forward to moving quickly.

— Olga Petrov
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0198

Attachments: shopwise_prompt_set_v1.csv (CSV, 12 KB); ab_matrix_proposal.md (Markdown, 4 KB)

From: Claire Jensen <claire@shopwise.com>

Cc: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@shopwise.com>
Date: 2027-05-31T09:07:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Shopwise call recap + proposed model-fit next steps

Hi Olga —

Thanks for the clear recap. We can share a labeled sample; Tom will drop a sanitized export to your S3 link by end of day Monday (6/1). A couple quick clarifications: 

- The baseline we want to beat is internally called "prod-v3" (noted in HubSpot). Can you make sure the comparison is run against that exact checkpoint?
- For the latency constraint — mobile traffic is strict; if Variant B needs to be behind an async rerank we’re okay as long as top-3 is improved.

One ask: can you include a short doc describing how you compute NDCG and MRR (weighting, ties handling)? Procurement may want that for an internal cost-benefit memo.

Appreciate it,
Claire
Head of Search, Shopwise

> Great speaking with you today...

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-06-01T11:42:00-07:00
Subject: Shopwise: initial fit run plan + benchmarks we’ll produce

Team —

Claire will provide a 10k labeled sample (prod-v3 baseline). Below is the evaluation plan I’m proposing so we present clear, actionable results: 

Planned artifacts (deliver by 2027-06-02 EOD):
- NDCG@10 and MRR snapshot comparing: prod-v3 (baseline), LlamaX-7B-quant (Variant A), Falcon-40B-ptq (Variant B), Distil-rerank-3B (Variant C).
- Per-query latency distribution (P50/P95) estimated under your traffic profile using Redwood's profiler.
- Cost-per-query estimate (tokens + batching model) for each variant.
- Prompt set v1 (attached) used for generation + rerank scoring script and tie-breaking rules.
- A/B matrix proposal: two-stage canary (20% Variant A vs baseline, 5% Variant B shadowed), see ab_matrix_proposal.md.

Notes on eval specifics (keep for the deliverable):
- NDCG: we will use graded relevance from your labels, discount base-2 log, ties handled with average rank.
- MRR: single relevant item per query; if multiple labels exist we take highest-relevance position.
- We will compute confidence intervals via bootstrap (1000 resamples) and report p-values.

Attachments to produce/attach: ndcg_mrr_snapshot_20270530.xlsx, shopwise_prompt_set_v1.csv, ab_matrix_proposal.md.

Neha — can you run the fit on the sandbox cluster (dedicated short job) and send me the raw CSVs and the summary workbook? Marcus — can you sanity-check the cost model and confirm latency estimates for LlamaX-7B-quant under your KV caching tweaks?

We should be conservative with Variant B’s live rollout given cost/latency. The plan in ab_matrix keeps it shadowed initially.

Thanks,
Olga

Attachments referenced: ndcg_mrr_snapshot_20270530.xlsx (XLSX, 85 KB)

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Jensen <claire@shopwise.com>, Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@shopwise.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-06-02T09:03:00-07:00
Subject: Shopwise: NDCG/MRR snapshot + proposed A/B matrix (attachments)

Hi Claire / Tom —

Attached are the results from the initial fit run we discussed. High-level takeaways: 

1) NDCG@10 and MRR (summary):
- Baseline (prod-v3): NDCG@10 = 0.421, MRR = 0.382
- Variant A (LlamaX-7B-quant): NDCG@10 = 0.447 (+6.1%), MRR = 0.407 (+6.5%) — statistically significant (p < 0.01)
- Variant B (Falcon-40B-ptq): NDCG@10 = 0.462 (+9.7%), MRR = 0.431 (+12.8%) — best quality, higher cost
- Variant C (Distil-rerank-3B): NDCG@10 = 0.433 (+2.9%), MRR = 0.392 (+2.6%) — low cost, modest lift

2) Latency & cost estimates (profiling on Redwood Dedicated):
- Variant A median latency 28 ms, P95 74 ms (within your 90 ms P95 target after KV cache tuning). Estimated incremental cost/query: $0.0019.
- Variant B median latency 62 ms, P95 160 ms (exceeds mobile P95 unless run async). Estimated incremental cost/query: $0.0048.
- Variant C median latency 18 ms, P95 62 ms. Estimated incremental cost/query: $0.0011.

3) Quality regression concerns:
- We saw a small cluster of query templates where Variant A underweights merchandising labels (example queries attached in the workbook). I flagged these and added a targeted prompt tweak in shopwise_prompt_set_v1.csv.
- Variant B is robust but has inconsistent tie-breaking on SKU-level duplicates; recommended to add a secondary deterministic heuristic for promo items during canary.

4) Proposed A/B matrix (high-level):
- Stage 1 (canary week 1): 20% traffic to Variant A vs 80% baseline. Monitor top-3 CTR, NDCG lift, conversion lifts.
- Stage 2 (shadow): 5% Variant B shadowed (no visible impact) while Variant A is live; collect quality telemetry and cost telemetry.
- Roll criteria: Variant A must maintain >= +4% NDCG and P95 latency <= 90 ms for 48 hours to expand to 50%. Variant B only promoted if top-3 conversion lifts justify async routing cost.

Attachments included: ndcg_mrr_snapshot_20270530.xlsx; shopwise_prompt_set_v1.csv; ab_matrix_proposal.md

Next steps:
- Claire: confirm you’re comfortable with Stage 1 starting week of 6/14.
- Tom: if procurement needs the NDCG/MRR computation doc, I can drop a short explainer by EOD.
- Redwood: we’ll prepare the canary playbook and monitoring dashboards (SLOs, regressions, alert hooks).

Thanks — happy to jump on the 30-min review if useful.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0198
